description: Host bridge for the two law-derived Accommodation Supplement inputs that rulespec-nz takes as inputs "for later cross-module wiring": the Social Security Regulations 2018 reg 17 base rate and the reg 18 non-beneficiary income cutout. Every rate comes from an engine evaluation of a bound rulespec-nz module; this resource declares only which outputs combine, with which coefficients and masks, under which input overrides, and the cutout's zero-solve. It ports the statutory branch (treasury_host_aligned false) of the axiom-oracles IncomeExplorer conformance harness. Method card MC11 makes it the one sanctioned exception to "real Axiom runtime only". When rulespec-nz encodes regs 17 and 18 (6 Oct plan B13), this resource and the bridge graph nodes are to be deleted, and only the Accommodation Supplement branches will re-run.
status: MC11 adopted (d1043). The graph executes both outputs through simulate.counterfactual@1 and simulate.solve_zero@1 with no new kernel.

source.plan_citation: The plan cites lines 1695-1790 of the same file at 302e43bafe5268448da3f3e16047832c1a3b736c on branch launch/ga-path-execution-gate, which is not on ops main. The composition is the same; main aggregates the per-adult zero-income amounts through aggregate_family where the branch sums them directly.

outputs.placement: Each scenario and variant branch runs its own base-rate node on its own population, so the S5 alternative owns its column without a rewrite.

input_overrides.reason: one eldest-child care unit, so the prescribed amount equals family_tax_credit_eldest_child_annual_amount (the parameter the harness reads, run.py:1525-1527)
harness constant for IncomeExplorer stylized adults (run.py:1941); open item: whether reg 17 uses each adult's own age-dependent rate is unresolved (reg 17 text not read in this lane)
harness constant (run.py:1947); superannuitant units follow superannuitant_units below

harness: family_shape youngest_child_age (run.py:1938,1951). The unit column is null for a childless family, and the engine adapter reads integer inputs as int64, so the override applies only where the unit has a dependent child; other rows keep the closure default 0.

terms.rule: a single unit takes the per-person zero-income amount once (run.py:2017-2024, 2545-2554)
a partnered unit takes it once for each partner (run.py:2017-2024, 2545-2554)

reg 17 adds the annual eldest-child family tax credit divided by 52 for a unit with a dependent child (run.py:2556-2562); the harness's 365/7 divisor is a Treasury-host diagnostic only and is not used

outputs.first_aggregation: Every Jobseeker input takes a unit value or a constant, so all members of a unit agree and first, the lowest person id, is safe.

outputs.legal_basis: Social Security Regulations 2018 reg 18; reg 18(3)(b) for sole parents
outputs.placement: The shared nz.as.bridge population, a FILTER branch of nz.as, runs the masks, the sole-parent gross rate and the cutout once for S0, S1, S2, S3 and S5; each variant repeats them on its own housing population.

gross_rate.rule: The engine evaluates the single-with-dependent-children rate under these overrides on every row, and the node writes it for sole parents only; other units read zero.

input_overrides.reason: below the 14-year threshold, so the gross rate is jobseeker_support_single_with_dependent_children_weekly_rate
the gross rate does not depend on income

solve.iteration_check: ldexp(5000, -43) is 5.7e-10, within the 1e-9 tolerance the kernel requires.
solve.quantization: none: the cutout stays a plain float64 input to the Accommodation Supplement engine

input_overrides.reason: harness constant for IncomeExplorer stylized adults (run.py:1941); open item: whether reg 17 uses each adult's own age-dependent rate is unresolved (reg 17 text not read in this lane)
harness constant (run.py:1947); superannuitant units follow superannuitant_units below

Holds for a single unit with no dependent child. On every unit except a sole parent it equals not partner_present (run.py:1948). A sole parent reads false, and with every partner flag false the reduction falls to its final else, Income Test 3, as reg 18(3)(b) requires.

harness: family_shape youngest_child_age (run.py:1938,1951). The unit column is null for a childless family, and the engine adapter reads integer inputs as int64, so the override applies only where the unit has a dependent child; other rows keep the closure default 0.

branches.residual: sole-parent gross rate minus the Income Test 3 reduction at the trial income
branches.legal_reading: Reg 18(3)(b) sets the income level as the income that would prevent payment of Jobseeker Support at the sole-parent rate as if Income Test 3 applied to that rate instead of Income Test 1. That income is the zero of the sole-parent rate minus the Income Test 3 reduction.
branches.equivalence: With reduction r(x) = max(0, x - L) * s, gross rate G > 0 and slope s > 0, the zero of G - r(x) is L + G / s, the harness expression.

branches.residual: the unit's own Jobseeker Support net payment at the trial income
branches.harness_expression: 500 + payment_at_anchor / (payment_at_anchor - payment_after_step), with the payment evaluated at weekly incomes 500 and 501
branches.equivalence: Income Tests 3 and 4 each have one rate, so the payment falls linearly to its zero and the harness's anchor extrapolation equals that zero. The solve also covers a zero anchor payment, where the extrapolation refuses; a positive residual at the bracket's upper end now refuses in place of the old slope check.

mask_note: Kernel masks compare equality only, so one calibration.prepare@1 node per population writes these family booleans ahead of the bridge nodes.

superannuitant_units.status: The harness has no NZ Superannuation or Veteran's Pension base-rate branch. G7 implements one from the reg 17 text if it can; otherwise the MC11 fallback stands: superannuitant units are excluded from the central run and counted. Scenario S5 carries the alternative. Awaiting D1 (MC11).
superannuitant_units.predicate_note: MC11 exclude-and-count and reporting must select this one assigned-member receipt predicate. A bridge implementation must resolve the reference rather than infer superannuitants from entitlement or age.

beneficiary_note: The harness computes the base rate from zero-income Jobseeker Support for every scenario, beneficiary or not; accommodation_supplement_non_beneficiary itself comes from the receipt layer through the group encode, not from this bridge.

cases.tolerance_note: decimal strings as committed; float64 graph columns reproduce them within a tolerance G7 states
